name: Public pages and store listings people see before they sign up

failureModes.prompt: Must a privacy policy and terms of use be published before the first person signs up?
failureModes.why: people must be told what is collected before it is collected, and both app stores require a privacy policy link

options.label: Published before sign-up opens
options.consequence: some writing before launch, and store review and payment setup can proceed

options.label: Add them after launch
options.consequence: a faster launch, and the store can reject the app until they exist

failureModes.provenBy: a check that the privacy policy and terms pages load from the public site and are linked from the sign-up screen and the store listing

failureModes.prompt: Should the store privacy labels come from a check of what the app actually collects?
failureModes.why: Apple and Google require the labels to include data taken by outside tools inside the app, and a wrong label is a breach of store policy

options.label: Check the code and services first
options.consequence: an hour of checking, and the labels match what the app does

options.label: Fill them in from memory
options.consequence: quicker, and a wrong label can get the app removed from the store

failureModes.recommended: Check the code and services first
failureModes.provenBy: a list of every outside tool in the app with the data each one collects, compared line by line with the submitted labels

failureModes.prompt: Should public pages describe only features that are switched on for everyone today?
failureModes.why: people who sign up for a feature they cannot find ask for refunds or leave, and some will say the page misled them

options.label: Only features live for everyone
options.consequence: a shorter list, and every claim on the page can be checked

options.label: Upcoming features, clearly labelled
options.consequence: shows what is planned, and each label needs updating when plans change

failureModes.provenBy: a review of each feature claimed on the public pages against the feature switches, with every claimed feature on for everyone

failureModes.prompt: Should the prices and limits on the pricing page come from the same place billing uses?
failureModes.why: a page that shows a different price or limit from what billing charges leads to refund requests and complaints

options.label: One source for both
options.consequence: a price change updates both, and the page cannot show what billing does not do

options.label: Write the page by hand
options.consequence: quicker to edit, and the page can show a price billing does not charge

failureModes.provenBy: a test that reads each plan's price and limits from billing and asserts the pricing page shows the same values

failureModes.prompt: When someone taps the main button on a phone, where should it take them?
failureModes.why: many visitors open links on phones inside another app's browser, where some sign-in and payment steps do not work

options.label: Into the app, or its store page
options.consequence: one tap to the right place, and app links need setting up for both stores

options.label: A web sign-up that works on phones
options.consequence: one path for everyone, and people who use the app see a web form first

failureModes.recommended: Into the app, or its store page
failureModes.provenBy: a recorded run on a real iPhone and a real Android phone, from a link opened inside another app's browser to a finished sign-up
